- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and news volume drops to 0, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect mean reversion.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (rapid changes >0.5) and news volume is low; add 0.5–1% to forecast to compensate for lag.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3–5% gap), model may be overconfident; apply a 1–2% downward bias for next forecast.
- When sentiment is high but recent price drops, model often fails to recognize reversal; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to align with sentiment shift.
